text:
Alex K: Heads-up — we saw a ~23% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for hosted models starting 2026-03-07 09:12 UTC. Spike lines up with tokenizer bump and a small system-prompt change. Dumping initial notes.

Priya S: Numbers?

Alex K: p50 requests: hit-rate 78% -> 55%. p95 similar direction. KV profiler shows many misses where the prefix string only differs in whitespace/field ordering. Also a tokenizer version change landed at 09:09.

Matt L: Was there a deploy at that time? @deploy-bot

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled infra/tokenizer:v2.3 -> v2.4 at 2026-03-07T09:09:12Z.

Jia W: We also started injecting a `tool_meta` JSON blob into the system prompt the previous day. That can change tokenization if not canonicalized (ordering + spacing).

Alex K: Repro'd locally: same prompt string but tokenized into different token ids across versions. That breaks prefix-keying because we currently use raw prompt bytes + model id in key.

Priya S: Can we fix without nuking cache? If we change the key, hit-rate drops more while caches repopulate.

Matt L: Plan suggestion: implement a migration fallback: compute new_key, try fetch; on miss, compute old_key and fetch; on old_key hit, write new_key. TTLs unchanged. That keeps warmness.

Alex K: Agreed. Short-term: include tokenizer-version + a normalized-tool-hash in the new key. Long-term: canonicalize system prompts (trim, stable-json, sorted fields).

Jia W: Minimal canonicalize I put in tests — passed on samples: 
```python
import json
def canonical_prompt(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        return obj.strip()
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return json.dumps({k: canonical_prompt(obj[k]) for k in sorted(obj)}, separators=(',',':'))
    return obj
```
This removed the JSON-ordering diffs and aligned tokenization across versions in unit runs.

ops-sre: Need an ops review for cache-key change and the fallback behavior. Fallback doubles lookup risk briefly; we should instrument and gate by canary region.

Priya S: Concrete rollout: (1) add tokenizer-version to cache key (2) implement fallback read-write migration for 48h in canary (3) run a warmup replay job over last 24h sampled requests (4) monitor hit-rate + cache.migration.fallback_hit metric + p99 latency.

Matt L: I'll open the runtime PR and the dashboard. Also propose a small sampling retention of original payloads for audit (sanitized).

Alex K: I'll add the migration metric and the backfill job spec. We'll keep old-key read as fallback only in canary/for 48h, then enable globally after verification.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started canary rollout of runtime/cache-migration at 2026-03-07T16:30:00Z on eng-canary.

Jia W: After ~2h warmup in canary: hit-rate recovered to 76% (from 55) in canary region, p99 latency stable. fallback_hit metric showed ~18% of reads used old-key and got promoted.

Priya S: Good signal. Follow-ups: add tokenizer-version to model metadata, add unit tests preventing prompt non-determinism, and schedule perf audit next week.

Alex K: Filed follow-ups: #1234 add canonicalization tests, #1235 dashboard + alerts, #1236 warmup backfill job. Will merge PR and proceed to gradual rollout if canary stays green.

Matt L: :thumbsup: will monitor dashboards.

Alex K: Closing thread when PR merged and canary metrics stable. Thanks all.
